fields.h1: Build a Demo Request Form That Books the Call on Submit
fields.hero_description: Build a demo request form that shows open times on submit and sends the prospect's answers to whoever runs the call.
fields.features_heading: What Happens Between Submit and the Demo
fields.features_subheading: A demo request form works when it ends in a booked call. These six pieces carry each request from the first field to the calendar.
fields.feature_1:
Open times right after submit

The prospect picks a 30-minute slot from the presenter's free times on the page that follows the form. A confirmation email goes out with the agenda and a calendar invite.
fields.feature_2:
A work email check before booking

A request sent from a personal email address gets a link to the recorded product tour in place of a live slot. Requests from work addresses go on to the booking step.
fields.feature_3:
Questions that shape the call

Ask for team size, the tool the prospect uses today and the two things they most want to see. Each answer is saved on the request, so the demo can be built around it.
fields.feature_4:
Answers in the presenter's inbox

The presenter gets an email or a Slack message with the prospect's answers as soon as a slot is booked. Nobody has to open the call by asking what the company does today.
fields.feature_5:
Every request in your own database

Each request is saved to a database you own. The app can also send it to HubSpot or any CRM with an API, with the booked time and every answer attached to the contact.
fields.feature_6:
Code that can live beside your site

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository. Run the form on your own servers next to the rest of the marketing site, and keep building on it there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Demo Requests, Start to Booked Call
fields.tab_content_1:
A Thursday slot is booked before the tab closes

Odalys Brennan wants a look at the reporting module from Fernmark Analytics. She submits the demo request form, and the next screen shows 5 open 30-minute slots with Caspian Reyes, the sales engineer. She picks Thursday at 2:30 pm. The confirmation email is in her inbox before she closes the tab.
fields.tab_content_2:
Personal email addresses go straight to a recorded tour

Last week Quarrystone HR received 40 demo requests. The form checks each email address on submit, and the 12 sent from personal addresses got the recorded tour by email. The other 28 went on to the booking calendar. Ravi Ostrander used his work address and booked a live call for Monday.
fields.tab_content_3:
Before the call, Marisol knows it is 85 trucks

Wren Haldane, a dispatcher at Tolland Freight, books a demo of Brightkeel Fleet Software. She answers the form's questions: 85 trucks, a shared spreadsheet, and route planning. Marisol Achterberg, the sales engineer, gets an email with those answers as soon as the slot is booked, and plans to open on route planning.
fields.tab_content_4:
An hour after a missed demo, three new times arrive

Harlow Ledger booked 18 demos this week. Of those, 14 have been held, 3 are still ahead, and 1 was missed. Teodora Vance never joined her Tuesday 10:00 am call. After 1 hour, the app emailed her 3 new times from the same presenter's calendar and moved her request to the rebooking step.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Demo Request Form
fields.howto_description: Follow 7 steps to build a demo request form that books each call on submit and gets the presenter ready for it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what a demo is for
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide who gets a live call and who gets the recorded tour. A three-person team trying a small add-on may only need the tour, while a company-wide rollout needs a sales engineer. Write that rule down before you pick a single field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for name, work email, and company on the first screen. Move team size and the current tool to a second step, after the prospect has started. Leave the phone number optional unless sales calls every prospect before the demo.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose two or three questions whose answers change the demo, such as fleet size, the tool in use today, or the feature the prospect wants to see first. Cut any question the presenter would not read before the call.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the presenter's calendar so the page after submit lists real open slots. Pick a length, such as 30 minutes, and a gap between calls. The prospect books on the spot instead of waiting for a reply by email.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the fields, the email check, the booking step, and the follow-up into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the screen the sales team works from, and changes any of it when you ask in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what happens when a prospect does not join. Set a wait, such as 1 hour, then send a fresh set of slots by email. Mark each request as held, upcoming, or missed, so the weekly count adds up.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one request from a personal address and one from a work address. Check that the first gets the tour by email, the second sees open slots, and the presenter's prep email lists every answer before the form goes live.

faq_plan.q: What is a demo request form?
faq_plan.a: A demo request form is the form a software or service company puts on its site for prospects who want a live walkthrough of the product. It asks who they are, where they work, and what they want to see. It should end with a booked meeting or a clear reply from sales.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a demo request form?
faq_plan.a: Settle who gets a live call, which answers the presenter needs, and what happens after submit. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form, the booking step, and the database that holds every request, then changes any piece when you ask.

faq_plan.q: Is a demo request form template enough, or should I build my own?
faq_plan.a: A template is enough when all you need is contact details and a message box. Build your own when the form has to book a time, check the email address, or brief the presenter. Start from a demo request form template, then add those steps one at a time. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: How is a demo request form different from a general inquiry form?
faq_plan.a: It has one job: get a prospect onto a sales call. A contact form takes any message, from support questions to press requests, and sends each to whoever handles that topic. Keeping the two apart means the people running demos never sort through billing questions.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a demo request form ask for?
faq_plan.a: Start with name, work email, company, and team size. Add the software they use now and the one thing they most want to see. Make the phone number optional. Anything the presenter will not read before the call can come off the form.

faq_plan.q: Should a demo request form accept personal email addresses?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but treat them as a separate path. Students and freelancers use personal addresses too, and they still deserve an answer. Reply to them with self-serve material, and keep the live calendar for requests from company domains.

faq_plan.q: Where should a demo request form go on a website?
faq_plan.a: Give it its own page, and link to it from the pricing page and the end of each product page. Keep it apart from a lead capture form for guides or webinars, which asks for less and does not promise a call.

faq_plan.q: Should a demo request form let prospects pick a time right away?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the presenter's calendar is kept current. Showing open slots on submit removes the emails it takes to agree on a time. Set a buffer between calls and a limit on how far ahead people can book. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API, including the calendar the sales team uses.

faq_plan.q: How quickly should a demo request form submission get a reply?
faq_plan.a: The same business day at the latest. When the form books the call on submit, the confirmation email is the first reply, and it goes out at once. Requests that need a person to review them first can still get an automatic email naming who will reply and when. Every request and its status are saved in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a demo request form sit next to a free trial signup?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the product can be tried without help. A sign up form opens the trial, and the demo request form serves buyers who want a guided call first. Put both on the pricing page, with one line under each saying who it is for.
